title: Running modulation ranks agree across gratings and scenes in 29 selected Allen mice
abstract: We tested whether the same neurons keep their ranks of running modulation across static gratings and natural scenes within mouse and visual cortical area. In 5,142 selected Allen Neuropixels units from 29 mice, the mean adjusted rank correlation was 0.394, with a 95% mouse-bootstrap interval of 0.354 to 0.433. All 29 mouse scores were positive. Controls included both block rates, waveform duration and four quality measures. Added Fano-factor controls and stricter filters kept positive estimates. Secondary pairs with drifting gratings or flashes also gave positive estimates. This supplies a same-cell state-coupling benchmark for structure-function models. Summary data cannot separate running from arousal, drift or common cell properties. No cell-level wiring, causal state effect, trial uncertainty or cross-species transfer was tested. Original code, aggregate results, source hashes and external retrieval steps are supplied. External source records are not bundled.

display.caption: Running modulation transfer within mouse and visual area. Points show mean rank correlations; bars show pointwise 95% mouse-bootstrap intervals. The unadjusted row is a rank correlation. Samples differ between filter and stimulus tests.

citations.reason: Builds on its within-mouse-area rank-transfer design for a distinct functional endpoint; no code or numeric table reused.
Regional structure-function analysis motivates a same-cell test of running modulation across stimuli.
